theme: 3 terms on ownership: a type that can never be copied, a parameter that only borrows a value, and a parameter that takes the value for good

terms.definition: A type marked `~Copyable`, so a value has only one owner and is moved instead of copied.
terms.example: Make the coupon a Noncopyable Type, so nobody can redeem it twice.

terms.definition: A parameter marked `borrowing` that can read a value for a moment while the caller keeps owning it.
terms.example: `show` only reads the ticket, so a Borrowing Parameter is enough.

terms.definition: A parameter marked `consuming` that takes ownership of a value, so the caller cannot use it afterwards.
terms.example: `redeem` should end the coupon, so give it a Consuming Parameter.

video.description:
Learn to explain ownership in Swift: Noncopyable Type, Borrowing Parameter & Consuming Parameter, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Noncopyable Type - A type marked `~Copyable`, so a value has only one owner and is moved instead of copied.
Borrowing Parameter - A parameter marked `borrowing` that can read a value for a moment while the caller keeps owning it.
Consuming Parameter - A parameter marked `consuming` that takes ownership of a value, so the caller cannot use it afterwards.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.description:
Explain Noncopyable Type, Borrowing Parameter & Consuming Parameter in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
복사 불가 타입, 빌려 쓰는 매개변수, 소비하는 매개변수 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Noncopyable Type - A type marked `~Copyable`, so a value has only one owner and is moved instead of copied.
한국어: 복사 불가 타입: `~Copyable`로 표시해서 값의 주인이 하나뿐이고 복사 대신 이동되는 타입

Borrowing Parameter - A parameter marked `borrowing` that can read a value for a moment while the caller keeps owning it.
한국어: 빌려 쓰는 매개변수: `borrowing`으로 표시해서 호출한 쪽이 소유권을 유지한 채 값을 잠깐 읽기만 하는 매개변수

Consuming Parameter - A parameter marked `consuming` that takes ownership of a value, so the caller cannot use it afterwards.
한국어: 소비하는 매개변수: `consuming`으로 표시해서 값의 소유권을 가져가므로 호출한 쪽이 그 뒤에 쓸 수 없는 매개변수

In this video, Mina and Jake figure out why a coupon must never be copied, which function only reads it and which one uses it up, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

dialogue.title: One coupon, one use

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, why does `Coupon` say tilde Copyable?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That makes it a Noncopyable Type. Nobody can make a second copy.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why would a coupon need that?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Each coupon works once. Two copies would mean two discounts.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: OK. And what does `borrowing` mean in `show`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's a Borrowing Parameter. `show` reads the `code`, but the caller keeps the coupon.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. A Consuming Parameter takes ownership, so the coupon ends inside `redeem`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No, the compiler stops you. Use the Borrowing Parameter first, then consume it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. A Noncopyable Type has one owner, and `redeem` is the end of the line.
A Noncopyable Type has exactly one owner, never a copy.
